statement: You are given a list of intervals, where intervals[i] = [start, end].
Return the minimum number of intervals you must remove so that the ones left over do not overlap. Intervals that only touch, such as [1, 2] and [2, 3], do not count as overlapping.

Greedily, sort the intervals by end and keep every interval that starts at or after the end of the last one kept. Ending early leaves the most room for the rest, so this keeps as many as possible, and everything not kept is removed.

examples.explanation: Removing [1, 3] leaves [1, 2], [2, 3] and [3, 4], which only touch at their ends.
Only one of the three copies of [1, 2] can stay, so two must go. [2, 4] and [4, 5] then fit after it.
The two intervals only share the point 2, so they already do not overlap.
